newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria warns Turkey against Iraq security zone.
newsitem.headline: Syria warns Turkey against Iraq security zone.

text.p: Syria on Sunday warned Turkey against setting a security zone in northern Iraq, saying this would put Ankara in conflict with Arab states and threaten the stability of the Middle East.
The official Syrian newspapers strongly condemned the Turkish plan as similar to the Israeli buffer zone in south Lebanon, accusing Washington of encouraging Turkey to take the decision.

"Insisting on this (setting the zone) no doubt would have negative results on future Arab-Turkish ties because Arabs would be forced to take the needed decision to protect their rights," the ruling party newspaper al-Baath said.

"The American raids on Iraqi targets encouraged Turkey...to take a decision on the heighest levels to set a buffer zone in the Iraqi lands under pretexts that are entirely unrelated to reality," al-Baath said.
Washington launched retaliatory raids against Iraqi military targets last week after Baghdad's troops entered Kurdish areas in northern Iraq to support a Kurdish rebel faction.

Turkey late last week said it was planning to set a security zone to push out Turkish Kurdish rebels who use northern Iraq as a base for attacks on southeast Turkey where they are fighting for self-rule.
The United States has said it backs the plan as long as it is temporary but France and Russia have come out against the proposal.
Another official newspaper, Tishreen, said the Turkish move was a threat to the security of Arab states and the stability of the Middle East.
"Any violation to the unity of the Iraqi land is a threat to the pan-Arab security and all Arabs," the paper said.
